column3: The Hebrew uses singular collective “the Canaanite” and ends “to fight against him.”
The Hebrew says singular “his hand”; BSB has plural “their hands.”
The Hebrew personifies Judah and his brother Simeon in the singular, with “me” and “I”; BSB uses the men of Judah, their brothers, and plural pronouns.
The Hebrew says Judah “went up” and uses singular collective ethnic names and singular “their hand.”
The Hebrew explicitly repeats Bezek and uses singular collective ethnic names.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew leaves the object of gathering unstated and does not explicitly say “to them.”
The Hebrew calls them “the sons of Judah” and retains the image “the mouth of the sword.”
The Hebrew uses singular collective “the Canaanite.”
The Hebrew explicitly names Hebron twice and uses singular collective “the Canaanite.”
The Hebrew has an unnamed singular subject, “he,” and explicitly repeats Debir.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew names an unnamed “he” as the giver rather than explicitly repeating Caleb.
The Hebrew leaves the woman and the man unnamed and says simply “when she came”; BSB names Acsah and Othniel and adds “one day.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew ends with singular verbs for going and dwelling; BSB uses plural “they.”
The Hebrew names Judah and his brother Simeon in the singular and uses a singular active naming verb; BSB pluralizes the people and makes the naming passive.
The Hebrew repeats “and its territory” for each of the three cities.
The Hebrew uses a singular subject for possessing the hill country and an elliptical clause without an explicit verb “could”; BSB uses “they” and supplies “could not.”
The Hebrew leaves the givers unnamed and says “as Moses spoke”; BSB names Judah and says “promised.” The Hebrew directly names the three sons of Anak, without “the descendants of.”
The Hebrew uses singular collective “the Jebusite” and explicitly repeats Jerusalem.
The Hebrew says the house of Joseph “went up”; BSB has “attacked.”
The Hebrew explicitly repeats “the house of Joseph.”
The Hebrew calls them watchers; BSB calls them spies.
The Hebrew uses an unnamed “he” for showing the entrance and the image “the mouth of the sword.”

The Hebrew repeatedly calls the dependent settlements “daughters” and uses singular collective “the Canaanite.”
The Hebrew uses singular collective “the Canaanite” and reinforces the negative expulsion with repetition of the verb.
The Hebrew uses singular collective “the Canaanite” and singular “his midst” for Ephraim.
